No doc_preflight.json sidecar exists anywhere in this plugin tree, so live fetch was the fallback. Version PASS: URL v-1-18-x, page header 'v1.18.x' vs target v1.18.0. Content PARTIAL: the endpoint, bodyless shape (only api-key header, no request body) and the 200 face ('successful operation', result:boolean) are documented, consistent with behavioral assertion; HOWEVER the state constraint's wording and the endpoint_registry doc_quote ('Removes cluster metadata and restarts as a single-node cluster from local data; irrecoverable for removed peers; use only when quorum is permanently lost') appear NOWHERE on the live v1.18.x page (live description: 'Attempts to restore or synchronize the node's current state with that of its peers.') and nowhere in the v1.18.0 source repo (repo OpenAPI summary 'Tries to recover current peer Raft state.', description absent, identical across redoc v1.3.x..v1.18.x). The Fern page documents only the 200 response; the repo's shipped openapi.json (docs/redoc/v1.18.x) additionally declares a 4XX error envelope plus a generic 'default: error' catch-all — no 5XX is explicitly documented. Endpoint precision PASS: endpoint_registry entry cluster+recover/POST exists with that source_url; raw_knowledge api_endpoints[] carries url=/cluster/recover; the script hit exactly that URL bodyless.

http_semantics.note: The request itself is well-formed (bodyless POST per documented params). The failure is a deployment-mode precondition (standalone, client-detectable via GET /cluster status:'disabled') surfaced as HTTP 500 + business error envelope 'Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode'. Inconsistent disposition class within the same API surface and same precondition: DELETE /cluster/peer/{peer_id} returns StorageError::bad_request('Distributed mode disabled.') -> HTTP 400 (src/actix/api/cluster_api.rs:108-111), while POST /cluster/recover and GET /cluster/metadata/keys return StorageError::service_error(...) -> HTTP 500 (cluster_api.rs:70 via toc get_consensus_proposal_sender; cluster_api.rs:125,146). Documented error face of this endpoint: 4XX envelope (repo OpenAPI) / none rendered (Fern v1.18.x page shows only 200).

Per the violates-declaration self-check the constraint citation was changed: the fired phenomenon is a disposition-face violation (documented face 200-only, observed HTTP 500 with a business error envelope), which engages the behavioral assertion (expected_behavior verbatim: 'HTTP 200 on cluster recovery (dangerous operational op)'); the state constraint qdrant_state_cluster_recover_001 (assertion verbatim: 'cluster recovery resets the peer to a single-node cluster from local data; it is destructive for cluster membership state') governs post-success state semantics and was UNEXERCISED — the op was refused, all no-op consistency legs passed (describe 200, count still 8, GET /cluster unchanged). api_violates_assertion=true is factual: a documented operation invoked per its documented parameters returned a status class outside the documented response face.

chain_trace.break_detail: Content-consistency break at the doc link: the contract's state-constraint semantics and its doc_quote are not substantiated by the cited v1.18.x page (live wording differs substantially: 'Attempts to restore or synchronize the node's current state with that of its peers.'). The behavioral 200 face IS documented, so the link is partial rather than absent. Additionally the Fern page documents no error responses at all, leaving the observed 500 outside every rendered documented disposition.

No gRPC face exists for this operation (grep recover_current_peer/RecoverCurrentPeer: actix + OpenAPI only).
source_grounding.verification_detail: A mode guard IS present and fires deterministically (get_consensus_proposal_sender errors when consensus is not enabled); the op is refused, never executed, and all data-plane state is preserved. The defect signal is not absent validation but the disposition class: a client-detectable deployment-mode precondition is raised as ServiceError/500 ('internal error') while the same file's remove_peer raises the identical precondition as BadRequest/400, and the cited doc page renders only a 200 face (repo OpenAPI: 200 + 4XX + default). No source comment, docstring, or maintainer note marks the 500-on-standalone as intentional (no 'by design'/'intentionally' annotation at cluster_api.rs:60-73, toc/mod.rs:546-551/775-779, or helpers.rs:247), so by_design_in_source is not available under the v3.4 tightened rule.

transport/environment failure (/healthz 200 before and after; error is a well-formed business envelope, not a connection failure)
mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode precondition: the target runs standalone (GET /cluster -> status:'disabled'); recover is a distributed-mode operation ('restore or synchronize... with peers' / 'recover Raft state') and cannot apply on this deployment, so the 500 is the deterministic product answer for this default deployment mode — whether the endpoint's behavior in standalone mode is an in-scope contract violation (vs a not-applicable face) is the auditor's judgment; the intra-codebase inconsistency (remove_peer 400 vs recover 500 for the identical precondition) and the undocumented-anywhere 500 disposition are the facts that cut against a clean not-applicable dismissal. Note also: the state constraint's post-success semantics are untestable on this deployment (op always refused), so the Type4 expectations in the meta oracle can never fire here.
